5-pt fit at 0deg obliquity (Bird & Livingston 2001 pp.60/62, via Wikipedia), <0.4% error. K-factor NOT sourced -- no published K-factor was found for this gun (unlike every other gun in this file); found instead via constrained least-squares search over K, requiring the fitted exponent stay within this project's other guns' physically-plausible range (0.8-3.0) rather than accepting the mathematically-best but non-physical fit (an unconstrained search found K=253 with exponent=15.8, rejected as degenerate -- see counters/toe/british_vehicles_1943.md and design note E.118). This is the first gun in this file whose K-factor is a constrained best-fit rather than a sourced or lightly-fit value -- flagged as a different, lower-confidence methodology tier.

11-pt fit vs RHA at 0deg obliquity (Bird & Livingston 2001 p.60, via Wikipedia), <0.4% error -- richest calibration set of any gun in this file. K-factor not sourced, found via the same constrained least-squares search as the 6pdr (see that row's note); this fit's exponent (1.24) fell within the physically-plausible range without needing the constraint to bind, unlike the 6pdr. Muzzle velocity flagged: a second Wikipedia-cited source (War Office pamphlet, 1952) gives 2950 fps instead of the 2900 fps used here (from the same table as the calibration points) -- used the value matching the calibration data's own source for internal consistency, not resolved which is more authoritative.

11-pt fit vs RHA at 0deg obliquity (Bird & Livingston 2001 p.60, via Wikipedia), <0.3% error. K-factor not sourced, same constrained-search methodology as the 6pdr/17pdr APCBC rows. Source notes APDS entered British service from March 1944 -- outside this project's nominal 1943 vehicle era; flagged for the designer to confirm in-scope before fielding on a 1943 roster. Discrepancy flagged 2026-09-12, design note E.132: a purchased Canadian Army TOE reference (MicroMark/Mark Bevis, List C3A) instead dates 17pdr APDS issue to 'Oct 1944' specifically for that unit. Not resolved -- plausibly a general-service-entry-date (March) vs. this-specific-unit's-actual-issue-date (October) distinction rather than a real conflict, but not confirmed either way; both dates postdate this project's 1943 window regardless.

4-pt fit at 30deg obliquity (Nachrichtenblatt zur Panzerbeschusstafel 7.5cm Pak 40 L/46, Nov 1942, via Wikipedia -- independently corroborated within 1-2mm by Panzerworld citing Geschossringbuch Band I), max 2.06% error -- looser than this project's vehicle-mounted German guns (5-pt fits at <1.2%) simply for having one fewer calibration point. K-factor NOT sourced -- no published value was found for this gun/round; found instead via the same constrained least-squares search used for the British 6pdr/17pdr (exponent held to the 0.8-3.0 physically-plausible band -- an unconstrained search found the same kind of degenerate solution those guns hit, K=223 with exponent=25.75, rejected for the same reason). This project's first towed anti-tank gun (as opposed to vehicle-mounted) -- see counters/toe/pak40_1943.md and design note E.123.

4-pt fit at 30deg obliquity (same Nachrichtenblatt source as the APCBC row above), max 0.66% error. K-factor not sourced, same constrained-search methodology as this row's APCBC sibling. Muzzle velocity flagged: a second source (Aberdeen/British Ordnance Board test data, Hoffschmidt 1979 via panzer-war.com) gives 933 m/s instead of the 990 m/s used here -- a real, unresolved ~3% discrepancy; used the value matching the calibration data's own source for internal consistency, same practice as this project's 17pdr APCBC note. Family hvap76 is a stand-in curve shared across German/Soviet 75-76mm-class tungsten rounds generally (a documented limitation of the source material, not of this project's fitting code) -- this is the first German gun in this file to actually use that stand-in.

5-pt fit at 0deg obliquity (Tank Archives 'americanized 6-pounder' blog, translating Soviet Lend-Lease testing data), 0.58% error -- tighter than this project's other unpublished-K-factor towed guns (PaK 40: 2.06%, 6pdr/17pdr: not separately reported). K-factor NOT sourced -- found via the same constrained least-squares search as the 6pdr/17pdr/PaK 40 (exponent held to the 0.8-3.0 physically-plausible band); the same degenerate pattern recurred (an unconstrained search finds a much higher, non-physical exponent for a similarly tiny error), and the constrained fit's exponent (2.94) again lands near the top of the plausible band, matching PaK 40 PzGr 39's own constrained exponent (2.94) almost exactly -- flagged as a recurring pattern for guns without a published K-factor, not a new anomaly. This is a 1943-SPECIFIC entry: the M1 is a licence-built near-copy of the British 6pdr (identical L/50 barrel) but fired only the uncapped AP Shot M70 until the capped M86/M85 shell arrived in late summer 1944 (counters/toe/us_57mm_at_1943.md) -- ammo_family is ap_uncapped, NOT capped, and this row should NOT be reused for a 1944+ US 57mm entry, which should use sixpdr_57l50_apcbc instead (near-identical MV, both capped, under 1% apart). This project's first use of the ap_uncapped family for an actual fielded gun.

5-pt fit at 0deg obliquity (Bird & Livingston 2001 pp.60/62, via Wikipedia), 0.22% error -- the tightest fit of any unpublished-K-factor gun in this file. K-factor NOT sourced -- found via the same constrained least-squares search as every other unsourced-K gun in this file; the exponent (2.26) landed comfortably within the 0.8-3.0 physically-plausible band without needing the constraint to bind, unlike the 6pdr's own APCBC row. This calibration data was already gathered and cited in counters/toe/british_vehicles_1943.md during the original British-vehicles research pass, but never added here -- surfaced by a 2026-09-12 cross-check against purchased reference material (Canadian Army TOE lists, MicroMark/Mark Bevis) that named 6pdr APDS as standard 1944-45 ammunition, prompting a check of this project's own prior research rather than new sourcing. Source notes APDS entered British service 'from March 1944' -- outside this project's nominal 1943 vehicle era; flagged for the designer to confirm in-scope before fielding on a 1943 roster, same caveat already carried by the 17pdr's own APDS row. See design note E.132.
